definition.name: Lighting dimmer
definition.description: Turn the knob to brighten or dim the reading lamp.

terminals.label: COM
terminals.purpose: COM is the bench name for this hole. In this lesson the feed comes in here. Either hole can take the feed on this dimmer.

terminals.label: OUT
terminals.purpose: OUT is the bench name for the hole used for the lamp wire. Turn the knob down and watch the lamp.

parts.name: Housing
parts.purpose: The case holds the working parts in place and keeps them apart.

parts.name: Removable cover
parts.purpose: Lift the cover on the bench to see the connections underneath.

parts.name: Terminal clamps
parts.purpose: A clamp holds the bare end of a wire against the metal terminal.

parts.name: Mounting and fixings
parts.purpose: These keep the fitting in place. Look for the screws or clips that hold it.

parts.name: Operating mechanism
parts.purpose: This part moves the contacts when you use the control.

parts.name: Control board
parts.purpose: The board takes signals in and controls the outputs. The bench shows what the board does at its terminals.

definition.abstraction: The bench uses a resistor to dim the lamp. Its resistance in ohms is 960 × (1/level − 1) + 0.001 at the default setting, with level between 0 and 1. At zero or when switched off, the circuit opens. The 960 Ω value comes from a 60 W lamp at 240 V. A real electronic dimmer switches part of each AC cycle. Use the maker’s figures for lamp compatibility and heat.
